messages:
tara: Quick q — thinking about slot affinity for Dedicated pools: binding conversational sessions to the same GPU slot to keep KV cache warm. Anyone seen p99 wins vs packing loss for 65B q4f16? sizing/ops impact? :thinking:
jon: We ran a microbench last week. Affinity lowered cold->warm p99 by ~18% on H100 for 65B q4f16, but packing efficiency dropped ~9% so throughput per GPU went down. Tradeoff is headroom vs unit cost.
maria: Do we have comparable numbers for A100 vs H100, and does autoscale headroom need to change if we flip affinity on?
kyle: A100 showed smaller p99 gains (~8%) since its kernel warm path is faster. Recommendation for Dedicated sizing for 65B quant: H100 -> target concurrency = 2, A100 -> target concurrency = 1. If enabling affinity, add +20–25% autoscale buffer for night/day burst variance.
ops-bot: sim-run: slot-affinity-experiment-1740607860 completed
ops-bot: summary: h100@eu-west: p50 180ms -> 170ms, p99 1.20s -> 0.98s; throughput -8%
ops-bot: summary: a100@us-west: p50 210ms -> 205ms, p99 1.05s -> 0.97s; throughput -4%
jon: Example command we used: ```./sim.sh --model 65b --quant q4f16 --gpu h100 --affinity true --concurrency 2 --duration 6h```
tara: Ok — that implies capacity sizing increases GPU count for the same QPS if we enable affinity. For Dedicated customers that want latency SLOs we should offer "affinity mode" as opt-in with clear unit-cost delta.
maria: I'll queue a 24h multi-region mixed-traffic sim (eu peak 12h / us peak 8h / apac low 4h) with autoscale burst modeling and kernel breakdown. Will attach charts when done.
kyle: flag: kernel fallback behavior when a slot hits saturation caused extra token-latency jitter in a few runs. Suggest canary ramp of affinity (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and tighten fallback thresholds. :thumbsup:
tara: Cool. Action items: @maria run the 24h sim, @eng-platform review oversubscribe/slotting heuristics, @kyle validate fallback kernel thresholds. Sync tomorrow to review charts.
